No. The Moon’s center is about **31.3° below the horizon**, so it is geometrically far beneath the Earth’s horizon and cannot be seen from Reykjavík at that time.

Clear skies, darkness, 11% illumination, and knowing where to look do not help when the Moon is below the horizon. Atmospheric refraction only shifts objects near the horizon by roughly **0.5°**, nowhere near enough to compensate for −31°. You would need to wait until after the Moon rises.
